subject: Nimbus Retail trial — success matrix, integration tasks & owners
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 15:20:00 +0000
Subject: Nimbus Retail trial — success matrix, integration tasks & owners

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned heading into the trial kickoff. I tried to keep this concise and actionable.

Summary of goals (from our convo):
- Real-time personalized recommendations in product search results (mobile + web).
- Reduce median recommendation latency and keep 95th p95 latency predictable under load.
- Measure relevance uplift vs. current baseline across A/B traffic slices.

Proposed success criteria (we'll finalize together):
1) Latency: 95th percentile inference latency < 150ms for 1k QPS synthetic load (mobile payloads).
2) Quality: MAP@10 improves by >= 8% on the evaluation set you provide.
3) Reliability: No more than 1.5% error rate across 7-day sustained test.
4) Cost target: inference token cost within agreed budget band (TBD after quantization/profile).

Trial evaluation plan (high level):
- Week 0 (this week): Exchange PII-free sample dataset + repo of evaluation prompts. (Action: Alice to share sample dataset by Tue 6/19)
- Week 1: Redwood staging deployment + SDK integration for streaming inference on a dev environment. (Owners: Jonas/Ben)
- Week 2: Run perf & quality runs; collect logs, token-level latency, and evaluation metrics. (Owners: Ben + Nimbus data engineer)
- Week 3: Joint review, iterate on batching/quantization profiles and run second pass.

Integration and implementation notes (technical):
- Preferred route: lightweight SDK (node/python) to attach to your recommendation service; we support streaming token responses for early-arrival scoring and function-calling for multi-step ranking.
- API surface: /v1/generate (streaming), /v1/embeddings for offline similarity precompute, and /v1/cache/keys for prefix caching. Ben will include a route map.
- Tooling: We recommend enabling KV cache + continuous batching for your expected session lengths to hit latency/cost targets.

Attachments: nimbus_trial_success_matrix.xlsx (draft success matrix), redwood_sdk_route_map.md (SDK/API route overview), sample-schema.json (expected request schema).

Asks / immediate next steps:
- Alice: share the anonymized sample dataset and who from your team will be the dev owner (name + calendar availability).
- Procurement: a single PO contact to expedite any trial contract / data processing addendum (if needed).
- Redwood: we will provision a staging token and a shared Drive folder by EOD Monday.

I copied Ben and Marissa for technical and commercial alignment. Thanks — I'll book a 30m kickoff once we have the dataset.

Cheers,
Jonas
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Nimbus Retail trial — success matrix, integration tasks & owners

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap and proposed cadence. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Data/residency: our legal team requires that PII be removed; we'll provide a redacted product/user interaction dataset by Tue 6/19 as requested. Can you confirm the staging environment will be in us-east-1 and that logs will be accessible only to designated Redwood engineers?

2) Dev owner: Tom Reyes (cc'd via procurement alias) will be primary for procurement; our dev owner for integration is Kara Jensen (not on this thread yet) — I'll add her after I confirm calendar windows.

3) Baseline metrics: we can share current MAP@10 and latency p95 numbers in the dataset doc; expect MAP@10 ~ 0.31 and backend p95 ~ 220ms.

We also have a follow-up question on streaming: do you support partial payloads (early scoring) where we can score top-K candidates and then call for full generation only for the top 3? That would be ideal to reduce cost.

I'll upload the dataset and a short baseline metrics doc to the Drive link you listed. Thanks — Alice
Head of Data Science
Nimbus Retail

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice@nimbusretail.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Nimbus Retail trial — success matrix, integration tasks & owners

Thanks Alice — good questions. Short answers and a couple of technical details: 

- Residency & access: yes, staging will be provisioned in us-east-1. We can grant token-scoped access to only the two Redwood engineers assigned to this trial; logs will be stored in a customer-scoped bucket with KMS key management. We'll include the logging ACLs in the onboarding doc.

- Streaming / early scoring: absolutely — we support a two-step pattern. Recommended flow:
  1) Call /v1/embeddings (or a light scoring endpoint) to compute vector scores for candidate set (batch embeddings).
  2) Use /v1/generate with streaming enabled only for top-K (we typically recommend K=3 for production cost/latency balance).
  3) Optionally use function-calling for post-processing (e.g., apply business rules, format templates) before returning to front-end.

- SDK route map: see attached redwood_sdk_route_map.md (we'll also drop examples in the Drive). Key route names you'll see: POST /v1/embeddings, WS /v1/stream/generate (for streaming tokens), POST /v1/rerank (for batch reranking).

- Quick perf tip: enable prefix KV caching for frequent user prefixes (session-level) to lower p95 under the burst profile you described. We'll share a short config snippet once we see sample request shapes.

I'm happy to schedule a short tech pair session with Kara once she's looped in.

—Ben
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
